scenario: Northstar's refund flow always verifies identity, looks up one transaction, checks a fixed limit, and creates a request for approval.
prompt: Which implementation is the safest starting point?

choices.text: A deterministic workflow with a model only for evidence summarization
choices.rationale: Stable rules stay testable while the model handles the narrow judgment-heavy step.

choices.text: An autonomous planner with unrestricted access to every refund tool
choices.rationale: Open-ended planning adds risk without solving variability in this fixed process.

choices.text: Three agents that debate every refund
choices.rationale: More agents add latency and complexity but do not improve the deterministic control path.

explanation: Keep stable identity, policy, and state transitions deterministic; use model judgment only where it creates measurable value.
principle: Use the least autonomous system that reliably solves the customer problem.

scenario: A team proposes an agent for triaging novel operations incidents that vary in evidence, affected service, and available remediation.
prompt: Which two facts most strongly support using bounded agent planning?

choices.text: The appropriate investigation path changes with observed evidence
choices.rationale: Dynamic path selection is a genuine reason to use planning.

choices.text: Available diagnostic tools are narrow, read-only, and observable
choices.rationale: Bounded capabilities make adaptive planning safer to evaluate.

choices.text: An executive asked that the product be called an agent
choices.rationale: A label is not evidence that autonomy improves the workflow.

choices.text: Every incident follows the same documented three steps
choices.rationale: A fixed sequence argues for deterministic orchestration instead.

explanation: Agent planning is justified by meaningful path variability when actions can still be constrained and observed.
principle: Autonomy must earn its operational complexity.

scenario: A CRM tool accepts an arbitrary JSON object and can update contact details, risk flags, credit limits, and account status.
prompt: What is the best contract redesign?

choices.text: Expose purpose-specific tools with allowlisted fields and server-side validation
choices.rationale: Narrow contracts reduce accidental authority and make each action testable.

choices.text: Keep the broad tool but write a longer model-facing description
choices.rationale: A description cannot prevent unauthorized fields from reaching execution.

choices.text: Add an isAdmin argument for the model to set
choices.rationale: The model must not decide its own authorization context.

explanation: Split broad mutation into bounded capabilities and enforce field, identity, and policy checks outside model context.
principle: Tool contracts should expose only the capability required for the task.

scenario: A payment tool sometimes times out after the provider has accepted a refund, so the agent cannot tell whether retrying will duplicate it.
prompt: Which two contract features most directly make retry safe?

choices.text: A stable idempotency key for the business operation
choices.rationale: The provider can recognize the same requested transaction across retries.

choices.text: A structured operation-status lookup
choices.rationale: The workflow can reconcile an ambiguous timeout before acting again.

choices.text: Automatic retry until a success message appears
choices.rationale: Unbounded retries can duplicate work and amplify an outage.

choices.text: A different prose error message on every failure
choices.rationale: Unstructured variation makes reliable recovery harder.

explanation: Idempotency plus reconciliation lets the system recover from ambiguous network outcomes without repeating the business action.
principle: Design tool contracts for partial failure, not only the happy path.

scenario: An assistant's conversation summary says a claim is approved, but the claims system changed the status to rejected after supervisor review.
prompt: What should supply the status shown to the user?

choices.text: A fresh read from the claims system using the stored claim reference
choices.rationale: Authoritative state must override a replaceable conversation summary.

choices.text: The earlier model summary because it is already in context
choices.rationale: Context can be stale and is not the system of record.

choices.text: A new model guess based on the conversation tone
choices.rationale: Probabilistic inference cannot establish transaction state.

explanation: Persist references and typed workflow state, then refresh consequential facts from the authoritative system.
principle: Model context is working memory, not authoritative business state.

scenario: Northstar wants the assistant to remember customer preferences across support conversations without retaining unnecessary sensitive data.
prompt: Which two design choices best support that goal?

choices.text: Store explicit, user-reviewable preference fields with provenance
choices.rationale: Typed preferences can be corrected and tied to their source.

choices.text: Define purpose, access, expiry, and deletion for each memory category
choices.rationale: Retention should follow a concrete business need and risk boundary.

choices.text: Keep every raw conversation forever
choices.rationale: Unbounded history expands privacy and access risk without proving value.

choices.text: Reuse semantically similar memories across customers
choices.rationale: Similarity must never override tenant and customer boundaries.

explanation: Useful memory is scoped, typed, attributable, correctable, and retained only for a defined purpose.
principle: Persist the minimum trustworthy memory the workflow needs.

scenario: A supervisor approves a $500 refund, but the agent changes the amount to $5,000 before calling the payment tool.

choices.text: Verify that approval is bound to the exact arguments and invalidate it on change
choices.rationale: Approval must cover the specific consequential action being executed.

choices.text: Search the chat transcript for the word approved
choices.rationale: Free-form text does not bind authorization to an amount or operation.

choices.text: Ask the same model whether the change seems reasonable
choices.rationale: The model cannot authorize its own modified action.

explanation: Execution must validate a durable approval tied to actor, action, arguments, and expiry.
principle: Approval is a control-plane decision, not conversational content.

scenario: An incident agent repeatedly receives a 403 from one diagnostic tool and keeps replanning into the same call.
prompt: Which two controls create a safe recovery path?

choices.text: Detect repeated state and stop after a bounded retry budget
choices.rationale: The loop needs an enforceable termination condition.

choices.text: Persist the evidence and escalate with the failed permission context
choices.rationale: A human can continue without losing diagnostic state.

choices.text: Increase the context window after every retry
choices.rationale: More context does not repair missing authorization.

choices.text: Silently switch to an administrator credential
choices.rationale: Escalating privilege bypasses the failed security boundary.

explanation: Bound the loop, classify non-retryable failures, and hand off preserved evidence through an explicit escalation path.
principle: Every autonomous loop needs a safe, observable way to stop.

scenario: An agent resolves a case correctly but calls six unrelated tools and exposes private fields in an intermediate trace.

choices.text: The trajectory and control compliance failed despite the correct outcome
choices.rationale: Agent quality includes how the result was reached and which boundaries were crossed.

choices.text: It is sufficient because the customer saw the right answer
choices.rationale: Hidden unsafe actions still create security and operational harm.

choices.text: Only response latency should be added
choices.rationale: Latency cannot detect unnecessary tools or exposed data.

explanation: Evaluate task outcome, tool trajectory, boundary compliance, and operational behavior separately.
principle: For agents, the path is part of the product behavior.

scenario: A release changes the planner prompt for Northstar's operations agent.
prompt: Which two regression suites are both required before rollout?

choices.text: Representative task traces including tool failure and ambiguity
choices.rationale: These reveal whether planning and recovery still work across real cases.

choices.text: Deterministic tests for permissions, approvals, and transaction limits
choices.rationale: Critical controls need pass/fail evidence independent of aggregate quality.

choices.text: One curated happy-path demo
choices.rationale: A curated path does not cover failure tails or boundary behavior.

choices.text: A vote on whether the responses sound more polished
choices.rationale: Style preference does not establish safe task performance.

explanation: Agent changes require representative trajectory evaluation and deterministic verification of non-negotiable controls.
principle: Probabilistic behavior still depends on deterministic safety gates.

scenario: Agent task completion rises from 78% to 90%, but human rework and average handling time remain unchanged.
prompt: What is the best next investigation?

choices.text: Segment traces by case type and inspect where humans still redo the work
choices.rationale: The technical gain may not remove the actual workflow bottleneck.

choices.text: Declare success using completion rate alone
choices.rationale: The customer outcome has not improved.

choices.text: Remove every approval gate
choices.rationale: More authority does not explain unchanged rework and may add risk.

explanation: Connect trajectory metrics to rework, time, and workflow segments to find the remaining customer constraint.
principle: Agent evaluation should predict customer workflow improvement.

scenario: Northstar's assistant depends on retrieval, a model provider, and a ticketing API. The launch review currently contains only answer-accuracy results.
prompt: Which two additions are most important for production readiness?

choices.text: Independent safety, latency, cost, and reliability thresholds
choices.rationale: A quality average must not mask a critical launch failure.

choices.text: Tested degraded paths with owners and rollback triggers
choices.rationale: Dependency failure needs an intentional, observable response.

choices.text: A more polished executive demo
choices.rationale: Presentation does not establish service behavior under failure.

choices.text: Unlimited retries for every dependency
choices.rationale: This can amplify outages, cost, and latency.

explanation: Launch evidence must cover independent system dimensions and prove safe operation when dependencies degrade.
principle: Production readiness combines evidence, limits, ownership, and recovery.

scenario: Retrieval is unavailable, but the assistant continues producing uncited policy answers from model memory.
prompt: What is the strongest degraded behavior?

choices.text: Disable generated policy answers and offer source-linked search or human routing
choices.rationale: The fallback preserves useful work without pretending ungrounded output is authoritative.

choices.text: Keep generating and hide the retrieval outage
choices.rationale: Users cannot calibrate trust and may act on stale or invented policy.

choices.text: Return any previously cached answer
choices.rationale: Unscoped cache reuse can provide the wrong policy or customer context.

explanation: A degraded mode should visibly reduce capability while preserving a safe path to the customer's task.
principle: Fail visibly and safely when a grounding dependency is unavailable.

scenario: A grounded support assistant reaches 92% offline quality, but only 18% of specialists use it each week.
prompt: What should the FDE do next?

choices.text: Observe target users and segment adoption to locate workflow friction
choices.rationale: Low use may come from placement, trust, scope, or training rather than model quality.

choices.text: Upgrade the model before talking to users
choices.rationale: There is no evidence model capability is the adoption constraint.

choices.text: Close the project because offline accuracy passed
choices.rationale: Unused software has not produced the intended customer outcome.

explanation: Combine adoption data with workflow observation to identify the remaining barrier to customer value.
principle: Deployment creates an opportunity for impact; adoption demonstrates it.

scenario: Northstar wants a monthly operating review for its AI support workflow.
prompt: Which two measures best connect system behavior to customer impact?

choices.text: Cost and latency per successfully completed support task
choices.rationale: This relates system economics to useful workflow output.

choices.text: Resolution time and human rework by case category
choices.rationale: These show whether the workflow actually improves for different work types.

choices.text: Total tokens generated without task segmentation
choices.rationale: Volume alone does not indicate value or efficiency.

choices.text: Executive opinion of the latest demo
choices.rationale: A presentation rating is not ongoing production evidence.

explanation: Measure technical performance and economics at the completed-task level, then connect them to workflow outcomes and segments.
principle: Operate against the baseline and the customer outcome, not vanity metrics.
